newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: IATA raps US plans to "over-tax" air travellers.
newsitem.headline: IATA raps US plans to "over-tax" air travellers.

text.p: The global airlines body IATA warned on Monday that the tax burden on international air travellers to and from the United States was set to soar if new U.S. congress proposals to raise airport taxes were enacted.

The Geneva- and Montreal-based International Air Transport Association said one Congress proposal would more than double U.S. international departure tax to $15.50 per passenger from $6 now and introduce a new international arrival tax of $15.50.

A second proposal agreed by the Senate Finance Committee called for setting the level of these two taxes at $8 per passenger but sought to introduce a new 10 percent levy on the value of U.S. domestic share of international journeys, it said.

IATA said it calculated the tax burden on international air travellers to and from the United States was expected to increase by between $10 billion and $15 billion over a period of 10 years if either of these proposals were enacted.
"IATA believes that air travellers are already over-taxed and that these proposals should not be enacted," it said.

"International airlines, through IATA, consider such action to be counter-productive," it said, adding the moves threatened to put future growth in the industry in jeopardy and hit profits of U.S. tourism and other businesses linked to air travel.
Industry data show world air traffic is booming partly thanks to a steady worldwide growth in leisure travel, with some 2.5 billion people passing through the world's airports in 1996.
